notes: Core facts match: one pale-haired figure in a sheer gown seated behind a draped stone ledge, a goblet raised in her hand, a row of goblets with pale liquid along the ledge in front of her, sheer fabric trailing over the ledge edge, white roses and blossoms at the lower left, wisteria framing the upper corners, a crescent moon, a domed colonnaded pavilion behind and to her right, and a bright reflected light path on the sea behind the ledge. The text declines to state a goblet count, which matches my own low confidence (I read roughly eight on the ledge with the leftmost clipped by the frame, plus the one held). Roses also appear at the lower right, and the ledge is more a curved sweep than a straight diagonal, but both are minor wording differences rather than factual errors. The one white bird I saw flying at the left over the water falls under the text's own flagged uncertainty about pale shapes being birds or clouds.

The poles themselves read as bare shafts with small twigs and leaves. The only thing hanging from a pole that I could resolve is a single small pendant near the top of the central figure's raised shaft. Some pale wisps near the upper left pole are indistinguishable from mist and the overhanging branches.

issues.existing: the central figure stands nearest the viewer, the others arranged in a loose ring around her

issues.evidence: All five heads sit on a shallow arc across the frame; the second and fourth are set slightly further back and higher in the haze, while the first and fifth are at the sides at roughly the central figure's depth. No figure is placed behind or on the far side of the central figure, which a ring arrangement would require. 'Nearest the viewer' for the central figure is defensible — she is the lowest and most fully rendered — but 'a loose ring around her' is not supported, and the haze makes depth cues weak enough that I could not establish the arrangement precisely either.

notes: The figure count of five matches my own count of five distinct heads. The X-shaped crossing of the poles in the upper centre, the crescent moon, the ruined columned arcade at the upper right, the shallow rippled water with floating petals, the flower crowns and the white blossoms at the lower left all match. The text's own flagged uncertainty about the exact pole count is appropriate: I could trace four shafts end to end and could not confirm whether one or two further segments are separate poles or occluded parts of those four. I read the disc as a clear crescent.

Strong match. The nine blades hanging point-down in a three-by-three grid of arched niches is confirmed — I resolved all nine individually, the bottom-centre one's hilt and upper blade being visible with only its tip occluded by the figure's bowed head. Also confirmed: one seated figure hunched at the desk with the head propped on one hand and a quill in the other over an open handwritten book; the lit lantern with a warm flame at the desk's left as the brightest warm point; an armillary sphere at the left edge and a second ringed sphere at the right, with a further round banded object low on the right that supports the text's reading of a globe; loose papers on the desk; gold constellation lines across the sky and inside the niches; a thin crescent moon at the upper left; water with a distant low treeline visible to either side of the niche wall; and the gold border with tick marks. The text's self-flagged uncertainties (small discs in the niches, paper and book counts, buildings versus trees on the horizon) match my own unresolved items — I also could not identify the small pointed structure on the left shore.
